newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma seeks further study on possible bourse.
newsitem.headline: Burma seeks further study on possible bourse.

text.p: Burma expects to commission several more foreign brokerages to study the possibility of opening a stock market in the country next year, Central Bank of Myanmar Governor Kyi Aye said on Friday.

The Burmese government is now working with Daiwa Research Institute to study the prospects of a new bourse to replace the country's current system of over-the-counter trading of company shares in the capital Rangoon.
Shares in about 300 Burmese companies are traded in the over-the-counter market, he told reporters while in Bangkok to attend the 32nd Southeast Asian central bank governors' conference.
The Burmese firms are mostly involved in foreign trading.
If Burma opened a proper stock market, trading would initially be conducted in the local kyat currency although foreign currencies could be introduced later, Kyi Aye said.
